After joining his fraternity he began smoking a lot of weed. I have smoked with him in the past but I always get paranoid and I don’t enjoy smoking. His frequent use was making me uncomfortable and I was worried about him and his future (he ended up being put on academic probation first term). 

One night that I was already in a super bad place emotionally I realized that he was smoking on a Wednesday after partying all weekend and Monday, with plans to party on Thursday or something like that. I called my mom crying about how I didn’t know what to do. I wrote him a letter because I didn’t want to verbally lash out and say things that I didn’t mean. 

I read it to him over FaceTime the next day after I had calmed down and decided that I stood by what I had written. I essentially told him that I was worried about him and that I didn’t know how it would affect our relationship. He started out being defensive and saying that he wasn’t worried because he only smokes after he’s done with homework and that the academic probation was a fluke and now he’s working extra hard. He thought that I should have no right to control what he does when we’re not together. I combatted by saying that even when we’re not together physically we are still in a relationship and I am just worried about it. 

After a few more discussions we have come to a compromise; he agreed to cut back to smoking 3 times a week and not smoke when we are together, period. It has been working out really well so far imo. I trust him fully and I know that he really cares about me. 

I just don’t know where the line is between controllling and concern is. I don’t want to be too controlling so I am glad that our current system works for us, but we both agree that ideally I can eventually get to a point where he can make his own choices about when to smoke or not.

So this year, we've got chocolate habanero plants on the grow, and since we're planning on using the strawberries for chili jams, WIBTA if we started rubbing chili on our unripened strawberries? 
We're thinking that it'd give the thieves a shock and deter them, but at the same time we're sure the culprits are kids and we're unsure about this.
